raw_segments.text: I thought of living there before I went to Walden.
I hooked the apples, leaped the brook, and scared the muskwash and the trout.
It was one of those afternoons which seem indefinitely long before one, in which many
events may happen, a large portion of our natural life, though it was already half spent
By the way there came up a shower, which compelled me to stand half an hour under a pine, piling
bows over my head, and wearing my handkerchief for a shed.
And when at length I had made one cast over the pickerel weed, standing up to my middle
in water, I found myself suddenly in the shadow of a cloud, and the thunder began to rumble
with such emphasis that I could do no more than listen to it.
The gods must be proud, thought I, with such forked flashes to rout a poor unarmed fisherman.
So I made haste for shelter to the nearest hut, which stood half a mile from any road,
but so much the nearer to the pond, and had long been uninhabited.
